savillsView.summary: Tokyo Grade A office demand remains robust driven by domestic corporate expansion and continued flight-to-quality. Prime rents in Marunouchi-Otemachi held at JPY 38,000–42,000/tsubo/month with vacancy compressing toward 2.5%. Occupier sentiment is positive with several large pre-commitments secured for 2027 completions. Limited new supply until 2027 supports landlord pricing power.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE reports Tokyo office vacancy declining to 3.1% in Q1 2026, with net absorption turning positive for the third consecutive quarter. Expects rents to edge up 2–3% over the next 12 months as supply pipeline remains constrained.

JLL highlights increasing demand from technology and financial services occupiers in central Tokyo, with Shinjuku and Shibuya submarkets seeing renewed leasing activity from domestic tech firms expanding headcount post-pandemic.
competitorIntel.source: JLL Japan Real Estate Intelligence Service Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank notes yield compression has paused at 3.5% for prime assets, with investors increasingly targeting value-add opportunities in inner suburban locations. Cross-border capital from Singapore and Korea remains active.
competitorIntel.source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Prime Office Rental Index Q1 2026

savillsView.summary: Greater Tokyo Bay Area logistics demand continues to outpace supply with vacancy at a record low of 1.8%. 3PL operators and e-commerce occupiers are driving absorption of large-format facilities (10,000 sqm+). Prime rents in Atsugi-Sagamihara corridor reached JPY 4,800/sqm/year. New completions in 2026 are largely pre-leased, sustaining tight conditions through year-end.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE forecasts the Greater Tokyo logistics market to remain undersupplied through 2027, with 85% of 2026 supply pre-leased at completion. Rents expected to grow 4–5% year-on-year.

JLL identifies cold-chain and pharmaceutical logistics as the fastest-growing sub-sectors, with occupiers paying a 15–20% rent premium for temperature-controlled facilities in Tokyo Outer Ring locations.

savillsView.summary: Luxury retail on Ginza and Omotesando continues to benefit from record inbound tourism, with Chinese and Southeast Asian visitor spending driving footfall above pre-COVID levels. Prime ground-floor rents on Ginza Chuo-dori stabilised at JPY 300,000/tsubo/month. International luxury brands are actively seeking flagship opportunities with limited availability keeping rents firm.

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank notes Ginza remains Asia's most expensive retail strip, with international luxury brands prioritising Tokyo over Hong Kong for APAC flagships given the city's tourism recovery and weak yen advantage for visitors.

savillsView.summary: Seoul CBD prime office rents remained stable at KRW 130,000–145,000/sqm/year as strong demand from financial services and tech tenants is offset by new supply entering the Gangnam and Yeouido submarkets. Vacancy in CBD remains below 5% but Yeouido is experiencing softening as tenants upgrade to newer GBD stock. Investment activity is cautious with buyers and sellers apart on pricing amid higher financing costs.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE flags rising incentives in Yeouido submarket as landlords compete for tenants relocating to newer GBD stock. Rent-free periods of 4–6 months being offered on new leases, effective rents diverging from headline figures.

JLL highlights global tech firms consolidating Seoul footprints into premium GBD towers, supporting rents above KRW 150,000/sqm/year in best-in-class GBD assets while legacy Yeouido stock faces headwinds.

savillsView.summary: Greater Seoul logistics market is experiencing a supply surge with 1.2m sqm of new completions in 2026. Vacancy has risen to 8.5% in secondary locations, though prime assets in Bucheon and Hanam corridors remain well-leased. E-commerce rationalisation has softened demand from pure-play online retailers, partially offset by growing 3PL and cold-chain occupier demand.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE reports effective rents under pressure in oversupplied corridors, with landlords offering fit-out contributions of KRW 50,000–80,000/sqm to secure anchor tenants in new completions.

savillsView.summary: Seoul is emerging as a priority data centre market driven by hyperscaler demand from Microsoft, Google and domestic players Kakao and Naver. Power constraints in the Sangam and Gasan clusters are pushing new developments to Incheon and Pyeongtaek. Colocation pricing has increased 10–12% year-on-year reflecting tight availability. Savills is tracking 450MW of announced capacity additions through 2027.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL forecasts Seoul data centre market to grow to over 800MW operational capacity by 2028, ranking it among the top 5 APAC markets. Power procurement lead times of 18–24 months remain the primary constraint on new supply.
competitorIntel.source: JLL Asia Pacific Data Centre Outlook 2026

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank notes Korean institutional investors are increasingly allocating to data centre assets, with cap rates compressing 30–40bps over the past 12 months despite the broader market caution.
competitorIntel.source: Knight Frank Korea Data Centre Investment 2026

savillsView.summary: Singapore Grade A office market continues to tighten with core CBD vacancy declining to 4.2% — the lowest since 2018. Prime rents reached SGD 14.50–16.00/sqft/month in Marina Bay and Raffles Place, with Savills tracking 15 active requirements above 20,000 sqft from financial services and wealth management firms. The pipeline to 2027 remains thin, supporting further rent growth of 5–8% over the next 12 months.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE records Marina Bay Financial Centre achieving SGD 16.50/sqft/month on recent renewals, setting a new benchmark for the market. Family offices and private equity firms are the most active demand drivers in H1 2026.
JLL highlights decentralised offices in Harbourfront and one-north continuing to attract technology occupiers seeking quality space at SGD 8–10/sqft/month, creating a two-tier market dynamic.
competitorIntel.source: JLL Singapore Property Market Monitor Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank forecasts Singapore prime office rents to grow 6–8% in 2026, outperforming the broader Asia-Pacific region, driven by limited completions and sustained demand from global financial institutions expanding Asia headquarters.
competitorIntel.source: Knight Frank Singapore Real Estate Highlights 2026

savillsView.summary: Singapore logistics market is characterised by chronic undersupply with JTC vacancy below 3%. Business park and high-tech industrial rents are rising sharply — prime rents at Mapletree Business City and one-north reached SGD 4.80–5.20/sqft/month. Semiconductor supply chain occupiers and biomedical manufacturers continue to absorb available space. Land-scarce conditions make new logistics development largely dependent on government allocation.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE notes ramp-up logistics facilities commanding a 20–25% premium over conventional warehouses, driven by e-commerce fulfilment and last-mile operators willing to pay for efficiency gains.

savillsView.summary: Singapore data centre market is constrained by the government's deliberate capacity management policy, with the development moratorium selectively lifted only for sustainability-compliant facilities. Available colocation capacity is at critically low levels, driving colocation prices to USD 200–220/kW/month for hyperscale deployments. Johor Bahru in Malaysia is emerging as an overflow market with strong cross-border connectivity to Singapore.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL identifies the Singapore-Johor corridor as Asia Pacific's most dynamic emerging data centre cluster, with over 2GW of planned capacity in Johor targeting Singapore overflow demand. Digital connectivity zone incentives are accelerating development timelines.
competitorIntel.source: JLL Asia Pacific Data Centre Outlook 2026

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank highlights Singapore data centre assets trading at sub-4% cap rates, among the lowest globally, reflecting perceived scarcity premium and long WAULT from hyperscale tenants.

savillsView.summary: Sydney CBD prime office market is bifurcating sharply — premium and A-grade rents held at AUD 1,500–1,800/sqm/year in the core with near-zero vacancy, while secondary and B-grade stock faces structural headwinds from hybrid working. Tenant demand is concentrated on ESG-compliant, amenity-rich buildings. Melbourne office market remains more challenged with effective CBD vacancy above 18%, though incentives appear to be stabilising at 35–40% gross face rent as the landlord community holds the line.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE data shows Sydney prime effective rents growing 4% year-on-year, outperforming all other Australian CBDs. Net face rents on premium floors approaching AUD 2,000/sqm/year in 1 Bligh and Salesforce Tower.

JLL flags Melbourne incentive packages averaging 42% of gross face rent, with some landlords offering 5-year rent-free on 10-year deals to secure anchor tenants in secondary buildings. Recovery timeline now pushed to 2028.
Knight Frank notes Brisbane emerging as an outperformer with sub-12% vacancy and rents growing 6% year-on-year, driven by infrastructure investment and interstate migration ahead of 2032 Olympics.
competitorIntel.source: Knight Frank Australia Real Estate Outlook 2026

savillsView.summary: Australian east coast logistics market delivered another strong quarter with prime super-prime vacancy at 1.2% in Sydney (South Sydney and Outer West) and 2.4% in Melbourne (Dandenong, Laverton). Prime net face rents in Sydney Outer West reached AUD 165–185/sqm/year, up 8% year-on-year. Land values continue to surge in land-constrained inner west Sydney. The development pipeline is elevated but much of 2026–2027 supply is pre-committed to large occupiers.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE records Sydney super-prime logistics achieving AUD 190/sqm/year net face rent in isolated cases, with refrigerated and automation-ready facilities commanding significant premiums over conventional dry warehouses.

JLL highlights Melbourne logistics continuing to attract interstate investment capital with yields ranging 4.75–5.25%, offering a meaningful premium over Sydney (4.50–4.75%) for comparable product quality.

savillsView.summary: Australian retail is experiencing a dichotomous market — neighbourhood and sub-regional centres anchored by non-discretionary tenants performing well with occupancy above 98%, while discretionary-heavy regional malls face softening specialty retailer confidence amid cost-of-living pressures. Prime CBD retail on Melbourne's Bourke Street Mall and Sydney's Pitt Street Mall has seen international fashion brands returning post-pandemic, with prime rents recovering toward AUD 12,000–15,000/sqm/year.

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank notes food and beverage operators driving neighbourhood centre rental growth, with quality food courts and restaurant precincts becoming the anchor offering for suburban centres replacing underperforming fashion tenants.
competitorIntel.source: Knight Frank Australian Retail Sector Report 2026

savillsView.summary: Hong Kong Grade A office market continues to navigate cyclical headwinds with overall vacancy stabilising at 13.5% following the departure wave of international tenants through 2022–2024. However, Central submarket is seeing selective demand recovery from mainland Chinese financial institutions, private wealth managers and family offices — a structural shift in the occupier mix. Prime Central rents have stabilised at HKD 80–95/sqft/month with further downside limited. Savills expects a slow, protracted recovery with rents recovering 3–5% by end-2026.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE data shows Central Grade A net effective rents 35% below 2019 peak levels, with limited prospect of rapid recovery given persistent hybrid working and occupier right-sizing. However, CBRE notes mainland financial firms now accounting for 38% of new leasing demand in Central, up from 15% in 2022.
competitorIntel.source: CBRE Hong Kong Office MarketView Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: JLL flags Kowloon East as a continuing beneficiary of flight-to-value from cost-conscious occupiers, with rents at HKD 28–35/sqft/month attracting professional services firms downsizing from Central while maintaining Hong Kong presence.
competitorIntel.source: JLL Hong Kong Property Market Monitor Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank highlights the Kai Tak commercial development emerging as a potential demand catalyst, with new government and infrastructure tenants anchoring the precinct and creating a new submarket with HKD 45–55/sqft/month initial asking rents.
competitorIntel.source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Real Estate Highlights 2026

savillsView.summary: Hong Kong logistics market remains supply-constrained with flatted factory and logistics warehouse vacancy below 4%. Modern ramp-up logistics in Tsuen Wan and Kwai Chung commands HKD 10–12/sqft/month with limited available space. Cross-border e-commerce with mainland China is the dominant demand driver. The proposed Northern Metropolis logistics hub is critical for future supply but remains a long-term project with first completions not expected until 2030.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE notes cross-border logistics operators maintaining HK facilities despite mainland China supply chain alternatives, citing Hong Kong's role as a re-export hub and established customs and legal framework advantages.
competitorIntel.source: CBRE Hong Kong Industrial MarketView Q1 2026

savillsView.summary: Hong Kong retail continues to face structural adjustment with total visitor arrivals still 25% below 2018 peak despite mainland tourist recovery. Causeway Bay and Tsim Sha Tsui prime rents are 40–50% below pre-pandemic levels but showing early stabilisation signals. Local consumption is supporting neighbourhood retail while luxury discretionary remains under pressure. The market is expected to remain in consolidation through 2026 with selective positive momentum in gateway malls.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL reports Causeway Bay retail vacancy declining marginally to 9.2% from a 2024 peak of 14.8%, with F&B operators and beauty retailers absorbing former fashion vacancies at rents 40% below pre-COVID levels.
competitorIntel.source: JLL Hong Kong Property Market Monitor Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank highlights luxury jewellery brands maintaining Hong Kong presence despite lower turnover, viewing the market as a critical China-facing window and strategic brand positioning location.
competitorIntel.source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Retail Report 2026

savillsView.summary: Hong Kong data centre market occupies a strategic but challenged position — strong connectivity to mainland China via submarine cables and dedicated cross-border links remain a key competitive advantage. However, geopolitical uncertainty has caused some hyperscalers to re-evaluate Hong Kong as a sole APAC hub, preferring Singapore or Tokyo as primary deployments. Savills sees sustained demand from mainland Chinese enterprises using Hong Kong as their international data gateway, supporting colocation prices of USD 130–150/kW/month.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL identifies Tseung Kwan O as Hong Kong's primary data centre cluster with over 200MW operational, noting that HKEX co-location demand and financial services latency requirements continue to underpin occupancy despite broader market uncertainty.
competitorIntel.source: JLL Asia Pacific Data Centre Outlook 2026

savillsView.summary: In Japan's office market, strong occupier demand, limited supply, and positive yield spreads continued to support pricing in Q1 2026, with prime office rents in Tokyo's Central 5 Wards touching new highs. Japan's commercial real estate investment reached JPY2.043 trillion in Q1 2026, up 2% YoY and the highest first-quarter level on record. Cross-border capital flows concentrated heavily in Japan during the quarter.

competitorIntel.summary: Tokyo's All-Grade office vacancy rate fell 0.1 pp QoQ to 1.5% in Q1 2026, with net absorption of 114,000 tsubo surpassing the new supply of 103,000 tsubo; Grade A and Grade A- rents both recorded their second-highest QoQ growth rates on record. In Osaka, the All-Grade vacancy rate declined to 2.0%, with Grade B rents surging 3.9% QoQ to JPY 16,150 — surpassing the previous peak set in Q1 2008. All-Grade rents rose in nine of the ten surveyed regional cities, with Sapporo, Saitama, Hiroshima, and Fukuoka continuing to set record highs.

JLL's city-level report on Tokyo's Grade A office market. Net absorption reached 69,000 tsubo in Q1 2026, up from 38,000 tsubo in Q4 2025, driven by employees returning to the office and business expansion in manufacturing, IT, and professional services. The vacancy rate held steady at 0.7% (down 1.8 pp YoY). The average monthly gross rent rose 5.2% QoQ and 13.2% YoY to JPY 40,247 per tsubo, reflecting near-zero vacancy and strong demand.

Knight Frank identifies Tokyo as the region's tightest prime office market in 2026, with Grade-A vacancy in the five central wards tightening to near-zero levels. Tokyo office rents rose 22% YoY in Q1 2026, the fastest rental growth across the Asia-Pacific region. New supply for 2026 and beyond remains extremely scant and pre-leasing is well advanced on available buildings, while the cap rate hovers around 3.5% for core office transactions.

competitorIntel.summary: The Greater Tokyo logistics vacancy rate decreased 0.6 pp QoQ to 9.2% in Q1 2026, with net absorption significantly surpassing the five-year quarterly average on strong demand for existing properties; effective rents rose 0.9% QoQ to JPY 4,530. Greater Osaka saw the vacancy rate fall sharply by 1.5 pp to 2.2%, with three new properties completing at full occupancy and effective rents rising 1.2% QoQ to JPY 4,350. Greater Nagoya vacancy increased to 16.8%, though effective rents still rose marginally to JPY 3,740.

JLL's city-level report on Greater Tokyo's logistics market. 3PL companies increasingly relocated and expanded logistics facilities throughout Greater Tokyo. As rents rose in core areas, demand for more affordable properties in fringe areas recovered. Overall vacancy declined 0.6 pp QoQ to 8.2%. The average gross rent was JPY 4,823 per tsubo per month (+0.9% QoQ). Capital values rose 0.1% QoQ and 1.2% YoY.

Knight Frank highlights Tokyo's logistics sector as resilient in 2026, with strong demand and rent increases expected to offset rising interest rates as the market gradually sees more CPI-linked contracts. Renewal rates remain high amid tight availability of super-prime logistics space in Greater Tokyo, while solid domestic consumption and flight-to-quality continue to drive expansionary demand. Supply chain diversification trends are broadening logistics demand beyond the Greater Tokyo area to regional markets.

competitorIntel.summary: Average rents set new all-time highs in five of the ten surveyed high street areas in Q1 2026 — Ginza, Omotesando/Harajuku, Shibuya, Shinsaibashi, and Kyoto — driven by fashion sector demand and new brand store openings. Vacancy in both Ginza and Shibuya remained at 0.0%, reflecting extremely tight supply conditions. Multiple retailers competing for single available units has become increasingly common, and CBRE expects average rents to continue on an upward trend.

Tokyo's prime retail markets of Ginza and Omotesando saw rents reach JPY 104,154 per tsubo per month in Q4 2025, up 1.9% quarter-on-quarter and 5.5% year-on-year, driven by international luxury brand expansion and strong inbound tourism. Capital values increased 1.7% quarter-on-quarter and 4.2% year-on-year as cap rates remained stable. Luxury goods sales resumed double-digit growth in November–December, with record foreign visitor arrivals supporting inbound consumption.
competitorIntel.source: Tokyo Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank identifies Tokyo retail rents as rising at the fastest pace across the Asia-Pacific region in 2026, up approximately 8% YoY, driven by record inbound tourism and strong domestic consumption. Japan's high street retail market is experiencing near-zero vacancy in major corridors including Ginza, Omotesando and Shinjuku. Rising inbound tourism and the depreciated yen continue to support luxury retail leasing demand at prime high-street locations.

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank identifies Tokyo as a primary APAC data centre market where AI adoption is driving unprecedented demand. With over 80% of 2026 capacity pre-let, supply remains constrained by construction costs and power availability, driving activity including the largest ever data centre financing transaction in Japan. Investors and operators are forming new joint-venture platforms to scale exposure into digital infrastructure.
competitorIntel.source: Tokyo Data Centre Market – Investment Outlook 2026

savillsView.summary: Occupancy rates across Tokyo's 23 Wards rose 0.6 percentage points QoQ to 96.8% in Q1 2026, driven by a return-to-office trend (companies offering remote work fell from 48.4% to 40.1% YoY). The central 5 wards recorded 96.4% occupancy, up 0.4 ppts both QoQ and YoY. Savills expects stable demographic fundamentals, the spring moving season, and rising condominium prices pushing renters into the leasing market to continue supporting demand. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: This research paper examines the factors driving investment concentration in the Greater Tokyo area, finding that Tokyo accounts for approximately 70% of total residential investment in Japan. The report identifies three key drivers: core investor criteria favouring Tokyo, high railway network density expanding suitable residential development areas, and rising university enrolment and urbanisation of employment. It notes a relative shortage of rental housing for low-income segments despite robust overall demand.
competitorIntel.source: Multiscale Analysis of Japan's Rental Apartments Market

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank's Prime Global Cities Index ranks Tokyo first among 46 global cities in prime residential price performance, with a 55.9% increase over the 12 months to Q3 2025. The outperformance is attributed to limited secondary market supply, strong foreign capital inflows and a persistent shortage of high-quality new developments. New condominium supply in 2026 is projected at approximately 23,000 units, the lowest level in more than 50 years, maintaining structural upward pressure.
competitorIntel.source: Tokyo Prime Residential Performance – Leading Global Markets

savillsView.summary: Savills Investment Management published analysis finding Japan's real estate market resilient despite Bank of Japan interest rate increases. The report concluded that office cap rates would only broadly shift with risk-free rates above 3.0%, a scenario considered unlikely. In the multifamily sector, demographic trends, urban concentration, and a strong preference for rental housing were identified as underpinning steady occupancy and predictable income streams. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE's Japan-specific results from the 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey indicate that the Japan investment market will remain active, with many investors expecting real estate prices to rise. A pronounced shift from core to value-add strategies was recorded, as rising interest rates are offset by strong rental growth prospects in the office sector. Investors are expected to focus on achieving returns through rental growth that exceeds the impact of rising interest rates and inflation-driven cost increases.
competitorIntel.source: 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey: Japan Results

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank highlights Japan as a core destination for global capital in 2026, driven by strong liquidity, low debt costs and strong inbound investor appetite following JPY 6.6 trillion in transaction volume in 2025. Q1 2026 volumes are 43% above the 10-year quarterly average. Japan accounts for over 80% of APAC living-sector volumes in Q1 2026, with new investors entering the multifamily market, while funding gaps in data centres are creating attractive private credit entry points.

savillsView.summary: Savills projects divergent vacancy trends across Seoul's major office districts as new CBD supply enters the market. CBD vacancy is expected to edge higher due to G1 Seoul and Rene Square completions, partially offset by expansions (Netflix, Bae Kim & Lee) and relocations at Grand Central. GBD vacancy should remain broadly stable despite tenant turnover, while YBD vacancy is set to rise short-term before improving as NH NongHyup Capital and Mirae Asset Securities take space at new buildings. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's city-level report on Seoul's office market. Overall quarterly net take-up reached 7,502 pyeong in Q1 2026, driven by CBD move-ins including NH NongHyup Tower occupancy. The Seoul vacancy rate fell 39 bps QoQ to 4.3%, with the CBD vacancy down 159 bps to 6.9%. Net effective rents rose 1.1% QoQ and 4.5% YoY to KRW 149,516 per pyeong. Total office investment volume reached KRW 3.4 trillion, highlighted by the ~KRW 1.3 trillion acquisition of Seoul Square.

Knight Frank identifies Seoul's Grade-A office market as supply-constrained, with the average vacancy rate across the three major business districts (CBD, Gangnam, Yeouido) at approximately 2.8% in Q1 2026. Tenants are adopting a wait-and-see stance ahead of large-scale new supply scheduled in the CBD in Q2 2026, including G1 Seoul and Re:nesquare. Rental growth is expected to persist as elevated development costs and rising asset values continue to widen the gap between prime and general Grade-A assets.

savillsView.summary: Savills Korea reported that South Korea's logistics investment reached a record KRW 5.7 trillion in 2025, up 16.8% year-on-year. Hard asset transactions alone totalled a record KRW 5.2 trillion, while distressed deals fell from 33% in 2024 to 19% in 2025. Foreign capital dominated at approximately 68% of total volume, with KKR acquiring approximately KRW 1.5 trillion worth of properties. Savills indicated the sector was approaching supply-demand equilibrium as new supply slows. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's city-level report on Seoul's SCA Grade A logistics market. Net absorption reached 33,652 pyeong in Q1 2026, with positive absorption in Central, North, South, and West submarkets while South-east was negative. The overall SCA vacancy rate was stable at approximately 15.4%. Net effective rents increased 0.7% QoQ and 3.2% YoY to KRW 32,600 per pyeong. Total logistics investment volume reached KRW 747.2 billion, with the quarter's most notable deal being the KRW 432 billion sale of Arenas Yeongjong.

Knight Frank reports that the Greater Seoul logistics market is expected to see Grade-A supply fall to its lowest level in a decade in 2026, driving rapid vacancy stabilisation toward the low-10% range from approximately 17% in 2025. 3PL providers and e-commerce operators account for approximately 77% of total demand. Ambient-temperature logistics vacancy has already fallen below 10% and prime assets are experiencing rental growth and asset value differentiation.

competitorIntel.summary: Seoul's prime retail markets saw modest rent growth of 0.4% quarter-on-quarter for both shopping malls and high streets in Q4 2025, with Myeongdong recording the strongest quarterly growth at 1.0% driven by surging tourist volumes. Shopping mall vacancy improved marginally by 20 bps quarter-on-quarter to 1.1%, while high street vacancy improved 68 bps to 14.5%. Both shopping mall and high street yields remained flat at 6.6% and 6.3% respectively as significant yield adjustments remain unlikely in the fragmented transaction market.
competitorIntel.source: Seoul Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)

competitorIntel.summary: JLL Research analysis of Korea's emerging co-living sector. Shifting demographics—including high home prices, risk of losing Jeonse deposits, high price-to-income ratios, growing single-person households, and long-term overseas visitors—have drawn foreign capital to Korea's co-living market. ICG's partnership with Homes Company established a co-living fund worth approximately KRW 300 billion. New LTV restrictions (0% in regulated areas) introduced in late 2025 are reshaping financing structures for rental housing operators.
competitorIntel.source: Foreign Investment Shapes Korea's Co-Living Market

savillsView.summary: Savills Korea reported that Seoul office investment reached a record KRW 21.1 trillion in 2025, surpassing the previous 2021 record of KRW 14.6 trillion. Q4 2025 alone accounted for approximately KRW 6.4 trillion. With several deals nearing closure and increased liquidity from domestic institutional blind funds including NPS and Korea Post, Savills projected 2026 transaction volumes to remain steady or see slight growth. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: Korean investor purchase intentions hit an all-time survey high in CBRE's 2026 Korea Investor Intentions Survey, reflecting strong sentiment across the domestic commercial real estate market. While 2026 investment volumes are forecast to moderate 5–10% from 2025's record KRW 34 trillion due to base effects, structural demand across office, data centres and logistics underpins resilient investor confidence. The survey highlights data centres strengthening as policy-driven strategic assets and prime office assets remaining the dominant transaction type.

South Korea's commercial real estate investment market achieved a record-breaking KRW 6.0 trillion in Q4 2025 office transactions alone, with the full-year 2025 figure reaching USD 28.1 billion (+29% year-on-year). Domestic asset management companies with dry powder from NPS, Korea Post and Yellow Umbrella Mutual Aid are expected to actively drive the investment market in 2026, alongside continued foreign interest in logistics assets. The CBD supply pipeline is expected to create an additional risk premium for investors and may redirect appetite towards Yeouido and Gangnam submarkets.

Knight Frank highlights South Korea as a two-way bridge for private credit capital, with domestic institutions allocating to global funds while foreign investors target approximately US$325 million in local real estate credit opportunities. Korea's commercial real estate market enters a mild correction phase in 2026 after a record 2025, but prime office assets remain the core of transaction activity. Data centres, hotels and alternative living sectors are broadening the investable universe for domestic and international capital.
competitorIntel.source: Seoul Capital Markets & Private Credit Outlook 2026

savillsView.summary: Savills Singapore revised its 2026 office rental growth forecast from 2% to 3%–5% YoY, citing persistently low vacancy levels and landlords' pricing power. CBD Grade A rents hit S$10.02 per sq ft — highest since Q4 2019 — while Grade AAA vacancy tightened to 5.1%. Shorter lease renewal terms are becoming more common among technology firms as companies navigate economic uncertainty. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's city-level report on Singapore's CBD office market. Positive leasing momentum from 2025 carried into Q1 2026, with vacancy tightening more significantly for prime properties. There were no major office completions during the quarter. Office rent growth continued, though quarter-on-quarter gains fell back to the sub-1% region. The Marina Bay submarket led the drop in vacancy rates, and some spaces were re-let before the current occupants vacated, reflecting strong demand for premium space.

Singapore office rents in the Central Region declined marginally by 0.2% QoQ in Q1 2026 per URA data, though prime Grade A CBD rents continued their recovery with islandwide office vacancy falling to 10.8% — its fourth consecutive quarter of improvement. Total available shadow space decreased by 2.3% to 422,000 sq ft NLA. The market continues to exhibit a flight-to-quality dynamic with premium Grade A buildings maintaining pricing power.

savillsView.summary: Strata industrial sales in Singapore declined 17.5% QoQ to 335 deals in Q1 2026, the lowest quarterly total since 2020, amid a more cautious business environment. Buyer preferences shifted sharply toward longer land tenures, with freehold industrial assets rising 2.9% QoQ to S$876 per sq ft and 60-year leasehold assets up 1.4% QoQ to S$569 per sq ft, while 30-year leasehold assets dipped 0.6% QoQ to S$353 per sq ft. Prime warehouse and logistics rents increased 0.4% QoQ to S$1.83 per sq ft per month. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's Q1 2026 report on Singapore's industrial and logistics sector. Demand held firm, with higher-specification logistics and warehouse premises remaining sought after. Islandwide average rents and capital values rose QoQ for the first time after six consecutive quarters of stability—ending a prolonged period of flat metrics. Yields were kept unchanged. Notable Q1 2026 deals included UI Boustead REIT acquiring three logistics assets for SGD 138.8 million and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT purchasing a facility for SGD 504.2 million. Capital value growth could outpace rental growth and tighten yields by year-end.

Singapore's industrial sector saw property prices grow at a slower pace in Q1 2026, led by multiple-user factories which posted a 1.7% quarterly increase. Demand for higher-specification logistics and warehouse premises remained healthy, underpinned by logistics service providers and e-commerce firms. The sector outlook remains supported by continual investor demand for quality logistics assets and Singapore's attractiveness as a safe investment haven.

JLL's Q1 2026 report on Melbourne's retail market. Both shopping mall and high street yields remained flat at 6.6% and 6.3% respectively as significant yield adjustments remain unlikely in the fragmented transaction market.

ICG's partnership with Homes Company established a co-living fund worth approximately KRW 300 billion. competitorIntel.summary: Korean investor purchase intentions hit an all-time survey high in CBRE's 2026 Korea Investor Intentions Survey, reflecting strong sentiment across the domestic commercial real estate market. While 2026 investment volumes are forecast to moderate 5–10% from 2025's record KRW 34 trillion due to base effects, structural demand across office, data centres and logistics underpins resilient investor confidence. The survey highlights data centres strengthening as policy-driven strategic assets and prime office assets remaining the dominant transaction type.

South Korea's commercial real estate investment market achieved a record-breaking KRW 6.0 trillion in Q4 2025 office transactions alone, with the full-year 2025 figure reaching USD 28.1 billion (+29% year-on-year). Domestic asset management companies with dry powder from NPS, Korea Post and Yellow Umbrella Mutual Aid are expected to actively drive the investment market in 2026, alongside continued foreign interest in logistics assets. The CBD supply pipeline is expected to create an additional risk premium for investors and may redirect appetite towards Yeouido and Gangnam submarkets.

Knight Frank highlights South Korea as a two-way bridge for private credit capital, with domestic institutions allocating to global funds while foreign investors target approximately US$325 million in local real estate credit opportunities. Korea's commercial real estate market enters a mild correction phase in 2026 after a record 2025, but prime office assets remain the core of transaction activity. Data centres, hotels and alternative living sectors are broadening the investable universe for domestic and international capital.
competitorIntel.source: Seoul Capital Markets & Private Credit Outlook 2026

savillsView.summary: Savills revised its Singapore office rental forecast for 2026 upward from 2% to 3%–5% YoY growth, supported by tight supply and sustained occupancy. CBD Grade A rents rose 0.6% QoQ to a post-2019 high of S$10.02 per sq ft (eighth consecutive quarter of gains), while Grade AAA rents reached S$13.28 per sq ft. CBD Grade A vacancy dipped to 6.6%, the lowest since Q3 2024, with Grade AAA vacancy falling to 5.1% for the fifth consecutive quarter. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's city-level report on Singapore's CBD office market. Positive leasing momentum from 2025 carried into Q1 2026, with vacancy tightening more significantly for prime properties. There were no major office completions during the quarter. Office rent growth continued, though quarter-on-quarter gains fell back to the sub-1% region. The Marina Bay submarket led the drop in vacancy rates, and some spaces were re-let before the current occupants vacated, reflecting strong demand for premium space.

Singapore office rents in the Central Region declined marginally by 0.2% QoQ in Q1 2026 per URA data, though prime Grade A CBD rents continued their recovery with islandwide office vacancy falling to 10.8% — its fourth consecutive quarter of improvement. Total available shadow space decreased by 2.3% to 422,000 sq ft NLA. The market continues to exhibit a flight-to-quality dynamic with premium Grade A buildings maintaining pricing power.

savillsView.summary: Strata industrial sales in Singapore declined 17.5% QoQ to 335 deals in Q1 2026, the lowest quarterly total since 2020, amid a more cautious business environment. Buyer preferences shifted sharply toward longer land tenures, with freehold industrial assets rising 2.9% QoQ to S$876 per sq ft and 60-year leasehold assets up 1.4% QoQ to S$569 per sq ft, while 30-year leasehold assets dipped 0.6% QoQ to S$353 per sq ft. Prime warehouse and logistics rents increased 0.4% QoQ to S$1.83 per sq ft per month. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's Q1 2026 report on Singapore's industrial and logistics sector. Demand held firm, with higher-specification logistics and warehouse premises remaining sought after. Islandwide average rents and capital values rose QoQ for the first time after six consecutive quarters of stability—ending a prolonged period of flat metrics. Yields were kept unchanged. Notable Q1 2026 deals included UI Boustead REIT acquiring three logistics assets for SGD 138.8 million and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT purchasing a facility for SGD 504.2 million. Capital value growth could outpace rental growth and tighten yields by year-end.

Singapore's industrial sector saw property prices grow at a slower pace in Q1 2026, led by multiple-user factories which posted a 1.7% quarterly increase. Demand for higher-specification logistics and warehouse premises remained healthy, underpinned by logistics service providers and e-commerce firms. The sector outlook remains supported by continual investor demand for quality logistics assets and Singapore's attractiveness as a safe investment haven.
competitorIntel.source: Singapore Industrial and Logistics Market Update Q1 2026

savillsView.summary: Singapore's retail vacancy rate held steady at 6.3% in Q1 2026, despite softer leasing demand and rising tenant churn, as the constrained supply pipeline (427,000 sq ft projected for 2026) contained vacancy. Prime Orchard Area mall rents edged up 0.1% QoQ to S$23.60 per sq ft, while suburban rents rose 0.2% QoQ to S$14.90 per sq ft. The market is bifurcating, with well-located prime malls maintaining occupancy while secondary locations face growing leasing challenges. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: Singapore's retail market saw occupier demand soften in Q4 2025 as the challenging operating environment and shifting consumer behaviours led retailers to seek more affordable options, though the Formula One race and year-end festivities provided a temporary boost. Islandwide vacancy rose quarter-on-quarter but remained contained as landlords prioritised occupancy, while prime floor space rents held stable on continued demand from quality-seeking occupiers. The suburban submarket recorded the highest vacancy increase of 0.1 percentage points driven by closures of underperforming stores at non-prime locations.
competitorIntel.source: Singapore Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)

competitorIntel.summary: Islandwide retail occupancy held steady in Q1 2026 despite several high-profile store closures, with vacancies quickly backfilled by new and existing brands. The retail sector continues to benefit from strong household spending, tourism recovery, and the flight of shoppers back to prime malls and street-level retail. Supply constraints continue to underpin rental stability in well-located assets.

savillsView.summary: Singapore developers launched approximately 1,844 new private units in Q1 2026, down ~30% QoQ and 41.3% YoY, while sales totalled ~2,025 units as demand outpaced new supply for a second consecutive quarter. Strong take-up was seen at River Modern (410 of 455 sold), Pinery Residences (537 of 588), and Newport Residences (184 of 246). Private residential prices rose 0.3% QoQ, moderating from 0.6% in Q4 2025. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: Singapore's prime non-landed residential market saw sales volume contract in Q4 2025, with October front-loaded by the launch of the 666-unit Skye at Holland. Prime resale non-landed home capital values rose on improved macro conditions and buyer preference for Prime assets as capital preservation vehicles. Luxury Prime rents fell amid weaker leasing demand while Typical Prime rents grew as cost-conscious tenants sought more affordable prime-district options.
competitorIntel.source: Singapore Residential Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)

competitorIntel.summary: Private home prices rose at a faster pace in Q1 2026, though overall sales activity softened. Rental prices rebounded marginally from a 0.5% QoQ drop in Q4 2025 to a 0.3% increase in Q1 2026. Executive Condominiums were the standout performer, with transaction volume tripling to approximately 1,500 units, while District 10 median prices surged over 40% driven by large-format freehold resale demand.

A healthy pipeline of investment-grade assets alongside sustained rental growth across key sectors should support growth in transaction volumes in 2026. competitorIntel.summary: Brisbane CBD prime gross face rents grew 3.7% QoQ and 9.2% YoY in Q1 2026, among the strongest performances in Australia, with incentives declining 50 bps to average 38.9%. Prime CBD yields tightened slightly by 2 bps to 7.02%, reflecting late 2025 transaction activity. Market sentiment is noticeably improved year-on-year, with more tenants engaging with the market, though rising bond rates and the cash rate are creating some near-term investment uncertainty.

JLL's Q1 2026 city-level report on Sydney's office market. The Sydney office vacancy rate remained flat over the quarter. One completion was recorded across all Sydney markets totalling 4,500 sqm. Office transactions were concentrated in the metro markets, with strong CBD leasing activity fuelled by occupier expansions and a continued flight-to-quality trend. The market is underpinned by very limited new construction and low pipeline supply.

Net effective rents in Sydney CBD rose 10.2% and Melbourne CBD rose 6.8% over the 12 months to end-March 2026 — the fastest post-pandemic growth rates. Brisbane CBD led with 11.7% annual net effective rental growth. Core precincts outperformed significantly: Sydney Core surged 14.3% and Melbourne Eastern Core jumped 16.1% YoY, creating a 54% and 93% premium respectively over non-core CBD locations.

competitorIntel.summary: Gross take-up in Australia's industrial and logistics market moderated to approximately 680,000 sqm in Q1 2026, with approximately 700,000 sqm delivered as the development pipeline remains elevated. National super prime midpoint yields expanded marginally to 5.7%, reflecting higher interest rates and elevated bond yields, while effective rents returned to growth as face rental growth began to offset elevated incentives. Close to 40% of the 2026-2027 supply pipeline is pre-committed, with investment sales for income-producing assets totalling close to A$1 billion.
competitorIntel.source: Australia Industrial and Logistics Figures Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's comprehensive industrial vacancy and supply update for Australia. Vacancy was broadly stable in Sydney, Melbourne, and Brisbane in Q1 2026. Sydney recorded 5.8% vacancy across 23.5 million sqm, Melbourne 5.2% across 30.6 million sqm (Australia's largest market), Brisbane 5.3% across 13.8 million sqm, and Perth the lowest nationally at 2.0%. Sub-lease vacancy decreased in Sydney (to 1.1%) and Melbourne (to 1.0%). The 45,000+ sqm cohort was the tightest nationally at 2.9% vacancy.
competitorIntel.source: Industrial Real Estate Market Analysis Q1 2026: Latest Industrial Vacancy Rates Across Australia

competitorIntel.summary: East coast industrial vacancy edged up marginally to 3.9% in Q1 2026, with Sydney recording the tightest rate at 2.9%. New supply is contracting sharply — 2026 completions are forecast to fall a further 20% following a 19% decline in 2025, totalling 1.66 million sq m. Brisbane leads on annual prime effective rent growth at 9.2%, and the thinning development pipeline is expected to drive stronger absorption and rental gains across east coast markets.

savillsView.summary: Australian retail investment volumes reached approximately A$4 billion in Q1 2026, the second consecutive quarter above that threshold, bringing rolling annual turnover to A$13.2 billion — up from A$9.9 billion a year earlier. Institutional capital accounted for 54% of acquisitions, while private and syndicated investors rose to 44%. Regional centres dominated at A$1.8 billion (nearly four times YoY), and neighbourhood centres rose 54% YoY, though large format retail was more selective. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: Net face rents grew across all retail sectors in Australia in Q1 2026, with CBD secondary and super prime assets recording the highest growth of 2.3% and 2.2% QoQ respectively. Shopping centre and large format yields continued to compress, with large format centres compressing 4 bps QoQ, while there were 32 retail transactions exceeding A$5 million totalling c.A$1.67 billion. Consumer sentiment declined significantly, with the Westpac-Melbourne Institute Index falling 12.5% to 80.1 in April amid global uncertainty.

JLL's Q1 2026 report on Melbourne's retail market. Non-discretionary spending increased 5% annually, double the discretionary spending growth of 2.7%, reflecting the ongoing polarisation in consumer spending. Six retail projects were completed in Q1 2026, up from the previous year. Eleven retail sales transactions occurred in Melbourne during the quarter. The market showed resilience in prime locations while secondary retail faced continued headwinds.

Australia's retail property sector delivered the strongest total return of all commercial property sectors in 2025 at 9.2%, carrying momentum into 2026 with around A$3.6 billion of retail transactions in Q1. Household spending growth and tightening supply are driving outperformance, though new geopolitical pressures from the Middle East conflict introduce uncertainty. Prime centres continue to outperform, supported by stronger sales, higher foot traffic and resilient tenant demand.

savillsView.summary: The first edition of Savills Australia's new monthly residential research update covering Australia's housing markets. The May 2026 edition focuses on the drivers behind Perth's continued price growth, Sydney's bifurcated market conditions, and key themes ahead of the Federal Budget. It serves as a regular pulse check bringing together data and on-the-ground market insight across Australia's increasingly uneven residential markets. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: CBRE's 2026 Pacific Market Outlook highlights Australia's living sector facing a structural supply shortfall, with apartment completions forecast at approximately 60,000 units annually—well below the long-run demand of 75–85k. Capital city vacancy is expected to decline from 1.8% in 2025 to 1.1% by 2030, with rents projected to grow +24% and capital values +28% over 2025–2030. Student accommodation and senior living remain under-penetrated, presenting significant investment opportunities amid demographic shifts and affordability pressures.
competitorIntel.source: CBRE Australia Pacific Market Outlook 2026 – Residential Sector

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's Q1 2026 city-level report on Melbourne's residential market. Apartment completions in Melbourne's inner precinct were just over 2,000 in 2025—a 10-year low. Median apartment sale prices in Melbourne remained largely stagnant at AUD 615,000 since early 2023. Apartment rents saw some modest growth. Buyer activity was increasing, supported by the constrained supply pipeline, with developers expected to deliver fewer new projects in the near term.

savillsView.summary: Savills forecasts prime Central office rents in Hong Kong to rise 5–7% in 2026, supported by tightening vacancy in the core Central submarket. Central Grade A rents rose approximately 3.5% in Q1 2026, with Central vacancy falling to around 9.9% by February — the lowest since 2023. Non-residential investment in Hong Kong was boosted by office and hotel deals, and investors explored hotel-to-student-accommodation repositioning opportunities. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: Hong Kong Grade A office rents increased 1.6% QoQ in Q1 2026 — the strongest growth since Q3 2018 — driven primarily by Central (+5.9% QoQ) and Greater Tsim Sha Tsui (+0.9% QoQ), with Grade A1 buildings in Central recording their strongest gains since Q3 2010 at +12.1% QoQ. No new supply was delivered this quarter, and with positive net absorption of 375,400 sq. ft. (a fourth consecutive positive quarter), overall vacancy fell 0.4 pp to 16.8%, the biggest single-quarter decline since Q2 2015. Over the past four quarters, cumulative net absorption has totalled 2.7 million sq. ft.

JLL's Q1 2026 analysis of Hong Kong's office market. Total net absorption reached 614,300 sqft but fell 59.7% QoQ from the elevated Q4 2025 base. The overall office vacancy rate stood at 13.5% at end-March; Central vacancy dropped 1.4 ppts QoQ to 9.6%—single-digit for the first time since 2023, driven by financial sector demand. Overall office rent rose 1.5% QoQ, with Central leading at +3.8% QoQ. Grade A capital values dipped 0.4% QoQ. Rents are projected to decline moderately by 0–5% in full-year 2026.
competitorIntel.source: Hong Kong Office Market Dynamics Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: This dedicated report examines the key demand drivers, occupier trends and market headwinds for the Hong Kong Island Grade-A office market heading into 2026. The report notes that premium Central Grade-A office buildings are expected to record positive rental growth of up to 8%, reflecting durable demand from financial services, family offices and Middle East capital diversifying into APAC hubs. A sharp reduction in new major supply from 2026 onward will provide the market with time to absorb leftover stock from 2024 and 2025.
competitorIntel.source: 2026 Outlook for Hong Kong Island Grade-A Office Market: From Volatility to Opportunity

Despite positive net absorption of 135,800 sq. ft. — ending four consecutive quarters of net withdrawal — overall warehouse rents fell a further 1.2% QoQ as landlords cut rates to improve occupancy, marking the ninth consecutive quarterly rental decline. Overall warehouse vacancy narrowed slightly by 0.3 pp to 12.8%.

JLL's Q1 2026 report on Hong Kong's industrial market. New lease activity remained constrained, supported primarily by the construction and semiconductor industries. Prime warehouse vacancy reached 10.5% in Q1 2026. Net absorption was negative for the ninth consecutive quarter, and there were no completions in Q1 2026. Investment activity was underpinned by an en-bloc transaction at Kodak House I and acquisitions by the Urban Renewal Authority, with mainland Chinese investors accounting for approximately 15.6% of total investment volume.

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank's quarterly summary analyses the performance of Hong Kong's industrial property markets. The report covers the logistics and warehousing sectors, tracking vacancy, rental and investment trends. Hong Kong's logistics sector is noted for its strategic relevance in the context of Knight Frank's Asia-Pacific Outlook 2026, which highlights Hong Kong's low-altitude economy and its impact on logistics demand across the territory.

savillsView.summary: Hong Kong's Tsim Sha Tsui retained its title as Asia's most expensive luxury retail location in the Savills ninth annual Global Luxury Retail Outlook, with annual rents of US$22,000 (approximately £16,160) per sq m — ranking as the world's second most expensive luxury retail strip after London's Bond Street (£19,228 per sq m). Hong Kong remained among the world's most active markets for new luxury store openings. The report noted slower rent growth in Hong Kong in 2025 compared to 2024's rebound. Prime yield: N/A. competitorIntel.summary: Leasing volume in Hong Kong's core retail districts totalled 213,800 sq. ft. in Q1 2026, declining QoQ due to seasonal factors but rising YoY; fashion brands were the second most active trade at 22% of volume, their highest share since Q4 2016. Low vacancy in prime areas pushed high street shop rents up 0.9% QoQ — the fifteenth consecutive quarterly increase — with vacancy for core retail districts rising slightly to 6.8%, still near its lowest since early 2024. Mainland Chinese tea and coffee shops continued to expand across the market.

JLL's Q1 2026 analysis of Hong Kong's retail property market. Retail leasing activity remained steady during the quarter. Prime shopping centre vacancy rose to 12.6% in Q1 2026. Investment volume dropped compared to Q4 2025, though the market has moved past its trough with retail sales recording sustained growth and high-street rents stabilising. Ongoing tenant reshuffling continued, with fresh concepts and F&B operators leading activity.
competitorIntel.source: Hong Kong Retail Market Dynamics Q1 2026

JLL's Q1 2026 overview of Hong Kong's residential market. Residential transaction volume rose 54.0% YoY in Q1 2026, with three residential sites tendered during the quarter. Luxury leasing and investment activity strengthened on the back of a broad market recovery, supported by easing financing conditions (HIBOR declining from 3.1% to 2.2%). The successful MTR Kam Sheung Road Phase Two tender reflected continued developer confidence in the Northern Metropolis.

Morgan Stanley raised its 2026 Hong Kong home-price growth estimate to 12%, citing strong sell-through rates, declining inventory, and falling land supply. Momentum is driven by a resurgent IPO market, mainland Chinese wealth inflows, and expanded talent visa schemes.

savillsView.summary: In Japan's office market, strong occupier demand, limited supply, and positive yield spreads continued to support pricing in Q1 2026, with prime office rents in Tokyo's Central 5 Wards touching new highs. Japan's commercial real estate investment reached JPY2.043 trillion in Q1 2026, up 2% YoY and the highest first-quarter level on record. Cross-border capital flows concentrated heavily in Japan during the quarter.

competitorIntel.summary: Tokyo's All-Grade office vacancy rate fell 0.1 pp QoQ to 1.5% in Q1 2026, with net absorption of 114,000 tsubo surpassing the new supply of 103,000 tsubo; Grade A and Grade A- rents both recorded their second-highest QoQ growth rates on record. In Osaka, the All-Grade vacancy rate declined to 2.0%, with Grade B rents surging 3.9% QoQ to JPY 16,150 — surpassing the previous peak set in Q1 2008. All-Grade rents rose in nine of the ten surveyed regional cities, with Sapporo, Saitama, Hiroshima, and Fukuoka continuing to set record highs.

JLL's city-level report on Tokyo's Grade A office market. Net absorption reached 69,000 tsubo in Q1 2026, up from 38,000 tsubo in Q4 2025, driven by employees returning to the office and business expansion in manufacturing, IT, and professional services. The vacancy rate held steady at 0.7% (down 1.8 pp YoY). The average monthly gross rent rose 5.2% QoQ and 13.2% YoY to JPY 40,247 per tsubo, reflecting near-zero vacancy and strong demand.

Knight Frank identifies Tokyo as the region's tightest prime office market in 2026, with Grade-A vacancy in the five central wards tightening to near-zero levels. Tokyo office rents rose 22% YoY in Q1 2026, the fastest rental growth across the Asia-Pacific region. New supply for 2026 and beyond remains extremely scant and pre-leasing is well advanced on available buildings, while the cap rate hovers around 3.5% for core office transactions.

Greater Osaka saw the vacancy rate fall sharply by 1.5 pp to 2.2%, with three new properties completing at full occupancy and effective rents rising 1.2% QoQ to JPY 4,350. JLL's city-level report on Greater Tokyo's logistics market. 3PL companies increasingly relocated and expanded logistics facilities throughout Greater Tokyo. The average gross rent was JPY 4,823 per tsubo per month (+0.9% QoQ). Capital values rose 0.1% QoQ and 1.2% YoY.

Renewal rates remain high amid tight availability of super-prime logistics space in Greater Tokyo, while solid domestic consumption and flight-to-quality continue to drive expansionary demand. Supply chain diversification trends are broadening logistics demand beyond the Greater Tokyo area to regional markets.

Tokyo's prime retail markets of Ginza and Omotesando saw rents reach JPY 104,154 per tsubo per month in Q4 2025, up 1.9% quarter-on-quarter and 5.5% year-on-year, driven by international luxury brand expansion and strong inbound tourism. Japan's high street retail market is experiencing near-zero vacancy in major corridors including Ginza, Omotesando and Shinjuku. Rising inbound tourism and the depreciated yen continue to support luxury retail leasing demand at prime high-street locations.

Investors and operators are forming new joint-venture platforms to scale exposure into digital infrastructure.

savillsView.summary: Savills Investment Management highlighted Japan's multifamily residential sector as demonstrating resilient fundamentals entering 2026, underpinned by demographic trends, urban concentration, and strong preference for rental housing. The report noted that even amid Bank of Japan rate increases, risk-free rates would likely need to exceed 3.0% before cap rates broadly shift. Steady occupancy and predictable income were expected to continue supporting multifamily investor returns. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: This research paper examines the factors driving investment concentration in the Greater Tokyo area, finding that Tokyo accounts for approximately 70% of total residential investment in Japan. The report identifies three key drivers: core investor criteria favouring Tokyo, high railway network density expanding suitable residential development areas, and rising university enrolment and urbanisation of employment. It notes a relative shortage of rental housing for low-income segments despite robust overall demand.
competitorIntel.source: Multiscale Analysis of Japan's Rental Apartments Market

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank's Prime Global Cities Index ranks Tokyo first among 46 global cities in prime residential price performance, with a 55.9% increase over the 12 months to Q3 2025. CBRE projects full-year 2026 residential prices to rise approximately 8% to 10%, supported by easing supply pressures and developer confidence.

JLL's Q1 2026 overview of Hong Kong's residential market. Residential transaction volume rose 54.0% YoY in Q1 2026, with three residential sites tendered during the quarter. Luxury leasing and investment activity strengthened on the back of a broad market recovery, supported by easing financing conditions (HIBOR declining from 3.1% to 2.2%). The successful MTR Kam Sheung Road Phase Two tender reflected continued developer confidence in the Northern Metropolis.
competitorIntel.source: Hong Kong Residential Market Dynamics Q1 2026

competitorIntel.summary: Hong Kong prime residential prices slipped 2.1% in 2025 per the PIRI 100, yet super-prime activity surged with 81 US$10 million+ transactions in Q4 — second globally only to Dubai. Morgan Stanley raised its 2026 Hong Kong home-price growth estimate to 12%, citing strong sell-through rates, declining inventory, and falling land supply. Momentum is driven by a resurgent IPO market, mainland Chinese wealth inflows, and expanded talent visa schemes.
competitorIntel.source: Hong Kong's Prime Market Turns a Corner

savillsView.summary: In Japan's office market, strong occupier demand, limited supply, and positive yield spreads continued to support pricing in Q1 2026, with prime office rents in Tokyo's Central 5 Wards touching new highs. Japan's commercial real estate investment reached JPY2.043 trillion in Q1 2026, up 2% YoY and the highest first-quarter level on record. Cross-border capital flows concentrated heavily in Japan during the quarter.

competitorIntel.summary: Tokyo's All-Grade office vacancy rate fell 0.1 pp QoQ to 1.5% in Q1 2026, with net absorption of 114,000 tsubo surpassing the new supply of 103,000 tsubo; Grade A and Grade A- rents both recorded their second-highest QoQ growth rates on record. In Osaka, the All-Grade vacancy rate declined to 2.0%, with Grade B rents surging 3.9% QoQ to JPY 16,150 — surpassing the previous peak set in Q1 2008. All-Grade rents rose in nine of the ten surveyed regional cities, with Sapporo, Saitama, Hiroshima, and Fukuoka continuing to set record highs.

JLL's city-level report on Tokyo's Grade A office market. Net absorption reached 69,000 tsubo in Q1 2026, up from 38,000 tsubo in Q4 2025, driven by employees returning to the office and business expansion in manufacturing, IT, and professional services. The vacancy rate held steady at 0.7% (down 1.8 pp YoY). The average monthly gross rent rose 5.2% QoQ and 13.2% YoY to JPY 40,247 per tsubo, reflecting near-zero vacancy and strong demand.

Knight Frank identifies Tokyo as the region's tightest prime office market in 2026, with Grade-A vacancy in the five central wards tightening to near-zero levels. Tokyo office rents rose 22% YoY in Q1 2026, the fastest rental growth across the Asia-Pacific region. New supply for 2026 and beyond remains extremely scant and pre-leasing is well advanced on available buildings, while the cap rate hovers around 3.5% for core office transactions.

competitorIntel.summary: The Greater Tokyo logistics vacancy rate decreased 0.6 pp QoQ to 9.2% in Q1 2026, with net absorption significantly surpassing the five-year quarterly average on strong demand for existing properties; effective rents rose 0.9% QoQ to JPY 4,530. Greater Osaka saw the vacancy rate fall sharply by 1.5 pp to 2.2%, with three new properties completing at full occupancy and effective rents rising 1.2% QoQ to JPY 4,350. Greater Nagoya vacancy increased to 16.8%, though effective rents still rose marginally to JPY 3,740.

JLL's city-level report on Greater Tokyo's logistics market. 3PL companies increasingly relocated and expanded logistics facilities throughout Greater Tokyo. As rents rose in core areas, demand for more affordable properties in fringe areas recovered. Overall vacancy declined 0.6 pp QoQ to 8.2%. The average gross rent was JPY 4,823 per tsubo per month (+0.9% QoQ). Capital values rose 0.1% QoQ and 1.2% YoY.

Knight Frank highlights Tokyo's logistics sector as resilient in 2026, with strong demand and rent increases expected to offset rising interest rates as the market gradually sees more CPI-linked contracts. Renewal rates remain high amid tight availability of super-prime logistics space in Greater Tokyo, while solid domestic consumption and flight-to-quality continue to drive expansionary demand. Supply chain diversification trends are broadening logistics demand beyond the Greater Tokyo area to regional markets.

competitorIntel.summary: Average rents set new all-time highs in five of the ten surveyed high street areas in Q1 2026 — Ginza, Omotesando/Harajuku, Shibuya, Shinsaibashi, and Kyoto — driven by fashion sector demand and new brand store openings. Vacancy in both Ginza and Shibuya remained at 0.0%, reflecting extremely tight supply conditions. Multiple retailers competing for single available units has become increasingly common, and CBRE expects average rents to continue on an upward trend.

Tokyo's prime retail markets of Ginza and Omotesando saw rents reach JPY 104,154 per tsubo per month in Q4 2025, up 1.9% quarter-on-quarter and 5.5% year-on-year, driven by international luxury brand expansion and strong inbound tourism. Capital values increased 1.7% quarter-on-quarter and 4.2% year-on-year as cap rates remained stable. Luxury goods sales resumed double-digit growth in November–December, with record foreign visitor arrivals supporting inbound consumption.

savillsView.summary: Savills Investment Management highlighted Japan's multifamily residential sector as demonstrating resilient fundamentals entering 2026, underpinned by demographic trends, urban concentration, and strong preference for rental housing. Steady occupancy and predictable income were expected to continue supporting multifamily investor returns. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

The report identifies three key drivers: core investor criteria favouring Tokyo, high railway network density expanding suitable residential development areas, and rising university enrolment and urbanisation of employment. It notes a relative shortage of rental housing for low-income segments despite robust overall demand.
competitorIntel.source: Multiscale Analysis of Japan's Rental Apartments Market

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank's Prime Global Cities Index ranks Tokyo first among 46 global cities in prime residential price performance, with a 55.9% increase over the 12 months to Q3 2025. The outperformance is attributed to limited secondary market supply, strong foreign capital inflows and a persistent shortage of high-quality new developments. New condominium supply in 2026 is projected at approximately 23,000 units, the lowest level in more than 50 years, maintaining structural upward pressure.

A pronounced shift from core to value-add strategies was recorded, as rising interest rates are offset by strong rental growth prospects in the office sector. Investors are expected to focus on achieving returns through rental growth that exceeds the impact of rising interest rates and inflation-driven cost increases.
competitorIntel.source: 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey: Japan Results

competitorIntel.summary: Knight Frank highlights Japan as a core destination for global capital in 2026, driven by strong liquidity, low debt costs and strong inbound investor appetite following JPY 6.6 trillion in transaction volume in 2025. Q1 2026 volumes are 43% above the 10-year quarterly average. Japan accounts for over 80% of APAC living-sector volumes in Q1 2026, with new investors entering the multifamily market, while funding gaps in data centres are creating attractive private credit entry points.

savillsView.summary: Seoul's prime office market recorded negative net absorption of -26,900 sq m in Q1 2026, pushing average vacancy up 0.4 percentage points QoQ to 4.0%. The CBD bore the brunt, with net absorption of -22,100 sq m and vacancy rising to 5.5%, while the Gangnam Business District was the only major submarket to post positive net absorption with vacancy stable at 1.7%. Redevelopment-driven relocations continued to shape YBD activity. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's city-level report on Seoul's office market. Overall quarterly net take-up reached 7,502 pyeong in Q1 2026, driven by CBD move-ins including NH NongHyup Tower occupancy. The Seoul vacancy rate fell 39 bps QoQ to 4.3%, with the CBD vacancy down 159 bps to 6.9%. Net effective rents rose 1.1% QoQ and 4.5% YoY to KRW 149,516 per pyeong. Total office investment volume reached KRW 3.4 trillion, highlighted by the ~KRW 1.3 trillion acquisition of Seoul Square.

Knight Frank identifies Seoul's Grade-A office market as supply-constrained, with the average vacancy rate across the three major business districts (CBD, Gangnam, Yeouido) at approximately 2.8% in Q1 2026. Tenants are adopting a wait-and-see stance ahead of large-scale new supply scheduled in the CBD in Q2 2026, including G1 Seoul and Re:nesquare. Rental growth is expected to persist as elevated development costs and rising asset values continue to widen the gap between prime and general Grade-A assets.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's city-level report on Seoul's SCA Grade A logistics market. Net absorption reached 33,652 pyeong in Q1 2026, with positive absorption in Central, North, South, and West submarkets while South-east was negative. The overall SCA vacancy rate was stable at approximately 15.4%. Net effective rents increased 0.7% QoQ and 3.2% YoY to KRW 32,600 per pyeong. Total logistics investment volume reached KRW 747.2 billion, with the quarter's most notable deal being the KRW 432 billion sale of Arenas Yeongjong.

Knight Frank reports that the Greater Seoul logistics market is expected to see Grade-A supply fall to its lowest level in a decade in 2026, driving rapid vacancy stabilisation toward the low-10% range from approximately 17% in 2025. 3PL providers and e-commerce operators account for approximately 77% of total demand. Ambient-temperature logistics vacancy has already fallen below 10% and prime assets are experiencing rental growth and asset value differentiation.

Shifting demographics—including high home prices, risk of losing Jeonse deposits, high price-to-income ratios, growing single-person households, and long-term overseas visitors—have drawn foreign capital to Korea's co-living market. ICG's partnership with Homes Company established a co-living fund worth approximately KRW 300 billion. competitorIntel.summary: Korean investor purchase intentions hit an all-time survey high in CBRE's 2026 Korea Investor Intentions Survey, reflecting strong sentiment across the domestic commercial real estate market. While 2026 investment volumes are forecast to moderate 5–10% from 2025's record KRW 34 trillion due to base effects, structural demand across office, data centres and logistics underpins resilient investor confidence. The survey highlights data centres strengthening as policy-driven strategic assets and prime office assets remaining the dominant transaction type.

South Korea's commercial real estate investment market achieved a record-breaking KRW 6.0 trillion in Q4 2025 office transactions alone, with the full-year 2025 figure reaching USD 28.1 billion (+29% year-on-year). Domestic asset management companies with dry powder from NPS, Korea Post and Yellow Umbrella Mutual Aid are expected to actively drive the investment market in 2026, alongside continued foreign interest in logistics assets. The CBD supply pipeline is expected to create an additional risk premium for investors and may redirect appetite towards Yeouido and Gangnam submarkets.

Knight Frank highlights South Korea as a two-way bridge for private credit capital, with domestic institutions allocating to global funds while foreign investors target approximately US$325 million in local real estate credit opportunities. Korea's commercial real estate market enters a mild correction phase in 2026 after a record 2025, but prime office assets remain the core of transaction activity. Data centres, hotels and alternative living sectors are broadening the investable universe for domestic and international capital.
competitorIntel.source: Seoul Capital Markets & Private Credit Outlook 2026

savillsView.summary: Savills revised its Singapore office rental forecast for 2026 upward from 2% to 3%–5% YoY growth, supported by tight supply and sustained occupancy. CBD Grade A rents rose 0.6% QoQ to a post-2019 high of S$10.02 per sq ft (eighth consecutive quarter of gains), while Grade AAA rents reached S$13.28 per sq ft. CBD Grade A vacancy dipped to 6.6%, the lowest since Q3 2024, with Grade AAA vacancy falling to 5.1% for the fifth consecutive quarter. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's city-level report on Singapore's CBD office market. Positive leasing momentum from 2025 carried into Q1 2026, with vacancy tightening more significantly for prime properties. There were no major office completions during the quarter. Office rent growth continued, though quarter-on-quarter gains fell back to the sub-1% region. The Marina Bay submarket led the drop in vacancy rates, and some spaces were re-let before the current occupants vacated, reflecting strong demand for premium space.

Singapore office rents in the Central Region declined marginally by 0.2% QoQ in Q1 2026 per URA data, though prime Grade A CBD rents continued their recovery with islandwide office vacancy falling to 10.8% — its fourth consecutive quarter of improvement. Total available shadow space decreased by 2.3% to 422,000 sq ft NLA. The market continues to exhibit a flight-to-quality dynamic with premium Grade A buildings maintaining pricing power.

savillsView.summary: Strata industrial sales in Singapore declined 17.5% QoQ to 335 deals in Q1 2026, the lowest quarterly total since 2020, amid a more cautious business environment. Buyer preferences shifted sharply toward longer land tenures, with freehold industrial assets rising 2.9% QoQ to S$876 per sq ft and 60-year leasehold assets up 1.4% QoQ to S$569 per sq ft, while 30-year leasehold assets dipped 0.6% QoQ to S$353 per sq ft. Prime warehouse and logistics rents increased 0.4% QoQ to S$1.83 per sq ft per month. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: JLL's Q1 2026 report on Singapore's industrial and logistics sector. Demand held firm, with higher-specification logistics and warehouse premises remaining sought after. Islandwide average rents and capital values rose QoQ for the first time after six consecutive quarters of stability—ending a prolonged period of flat metrics. Yields were kept unchanged. Notable Q1 2026 deals included UI Boustead REIT acquiring three logistics assets for SGD 138.8 million and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT purchasing a facility for SGD 504.2 million. Capital value growth could outpace rental growth and tighten yields by year-end.

Singapore's industrial sector saw property prices grow at a slower pace in Q1 2026, led by multiple-user factories which posted a 1.7% quarterly increase. Demand for higher-specification logistics and warehouse premises remained healthy, underpinned by logistics service providers and e-commerce firms. The sector outlook remains supported by continual investor demand for quality logistics assets and Singapore's attractiveness as a safe investment haven.
competitorIntel.source: Singapore Industrial and Logistics Market Update Q1 2026

savillsView.summary: Singapore's retail vacancy rate held steady at 6.3% in Q1 2026, despite softer leasing demand and rising tenant churn, as the constrained supply pipeline (427,000 sq ft projected for 2026) contained vacancy. Prime Orchard Area mall rents edged up 0.1% QoQ to S$23.60 per sq ft, while suburban rents rose 0.2% QoQ to S$14.90 per sq ft. The market is bifurcating, with well-located prime malls maintaining occupancy while secondary locations face growing leasing challenges. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: Singapore's retail market saw occupier demand soften in Q4 2025 as the challenging operating environment and shifting consumer behaviours led retailers to seek more affordable options, though the Formula One race and year-end festivities provided a temporary boost. Islandwide vacancy rose quarter-on-quarter but remained contained as landlords prioritised occupancy, while prime floor space rents held stable on continued demand from quality-seeking occupiers. The suburban submarket recorded the highest vacancy increase of 0.1 percentage points driven by closures of underperforming stores at non-prime locations.
competitorIntel.source: Singapore Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)

competitorIntel.summary: Islandwide retail occupancy held steady in Q1 2026 despite several high-profile store closures, with vacancies quickly backfilled by new and existing brands. The retail sector continues to benefit from strong household spending, tourism recovery, and the flight of shoppers back to prime malls and street-level retail. Supply constraints continue to underpin rental stability in well-located assets.

savillsView.summary: Singapore developers launched approximately 1,844 new private units in Q1 2026, down ~30% QoQ and 41.3% YoY, while sales totalled ~2,025 units as demand outpaced new supply for a second consecutive quarter. Strong take-up was seen at River Modern (410 of 455 sold), Pinery Residences (537 of 588), and Newport Residences (184 of 246). Private residential prices rose 0.3% QoQ, moderating from 0.6% in Q4 2025. Prime yield: N/A. Prime rent: N/A.

competitorIntel.summary: Singapore's prime non-landed residential market saw sales volume contract in Q4 2025, with October front-loaded by the launch of the 666-unit Skye at Holland. Prime resale non-landed home capital values rose on improved macro conditions and buyer preference for Prime assets as capital preservation vehicles. Luxury Prime rents fell amid weaker leasing demand while Typical Prime rents grew as cost-conscious tenants sought more affordable prime-district options.

Executive Condominiums were the standout performer, with transaction volume tripling to approximately 1,500 units, while District 10 median prices surged over 40% driven by large-format freehold resale demand.

A healthy pipeline of investment-grade assets alongside sustained rental growth across key sectors should support growth in transaction volumes in 2026.
